title: Research Confirms Tai Chi Health Benefits
paragraphs: Tai chi, a traditional Chinese form of exercise that involves slow, flowing movements, is practiced by millions of people around the world. Now, a major new review has provided strong evidence that tai chi and similar exercises can help people with a variety of conditions affecting the muscles, bones and joints.

The review, which was carried out by researchers from Liaoning, China, was published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine in August 2026. It was an "umbrella review," which means that it brought together the results of many previous reviews. In total, it included 92 analyses based on 1,744 randomized controlled trials. The review looked at several traditional Chinese exercises, including tai chi, qigong and baduanjin.

According to the review, there was "high certainty evidence" that these exercises improve a range of health outcomes. For example, they helped people with knee osteoarthritis move more easily, and tai chi in particular was found to reduce chronic pain and stiffness in muscles and joints. The exercises were also linked to better mental health in people with neck pain and knee osteoarthritis, as well as better sleep in people with fibromyalgia, a condition that causes pain throughout the body. In addition, tai chi was linked to improvements in bone density among people with weak bones.
The researchers found that the greatest benefits came when people practiced for more than six months, at least three times a week, for a total of at least 150 minutes a week.

According to the researchers, these exercises are safe, accessible and low-cost. They believe the exercises can be used alongside regular medical treatment, help reduce people's need for medication and support patients in managing their own conditions.

Other recent research has found further benefits. For example, a 2026 analysis published in the journal Scientific Reports suggested that tai chi may improve blood pressure, as well as people's physical fitness and mental well-being. However, the authors of that analysis noted that its conclusions should be interpreted with caution. Meanwhile, a separate review suggested that tai chi may help ease symptoms of depression, improve sleep and improve balance.
However, researchers say there is less evidence that tai chi can treat diagnosed anxiety disorders or reduce the risk of developing dementia.
